hints.title: Evaluate Orderings
hints.text: Consider the two possible execution orders: land before water or water before land.

hints.title: Sequential Start Offset
hints.text: The second ride cannot begin until both the first ride completes and the second ride's start time arrives.

hints.title: Pairwise Evaluation
hints.text: Iterate across all combinations of land rides and water rides, taking the minimum total completion timestamp.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def earliestFinishTime(self, landStartTime: List[int], landDuration: List[int], waterStartTime: List[int], waterDuration: List[int]) -> int:
        n_l = len(landStartTime)
        n_w = len(waterStartTime)
        best = float('inf')
        
        # Try every pair (i, j)
        for i in range(n_l):
            ls, ld = landStartTime[i], landDuration[i]
            l_finish = ls + ld
            for j in range(n_w):
                ws, wd = waterStartTime[j], waterDuration[j]
                w_finish = ws + wd
                
                # Land then water
                w_start_after_l = max(l_finish, ws)
                finish_lw = w_start_after_l + wd
                
                # Water then land
                l_start_after_w = max(w_finish, ls)
                finish_wl = l_start_after_w + ld
                
                best = min(best, finish_lw, finish_wl)
                
        return best
```

complexity.notes: Iterates through all ride pairs to determine the minimum finish time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute force pair inspection suffices for small constraint bounds of variant I.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Evaluates finish times in place without allocating extra collections.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize the two sequence orders and handle start availability using the maximum operator.
